attempts: Verify the pipeline order is corrected from sort→limit→filter to filter→sort→limit by checking that AC-2 (q=an&limit=2 returns [banana,mango] not [banana]) and AC-3 (q=an&sort=name&limit=1 returns [banana]) are satisfied

Verify the needle is correctly implemented as q.toLowerCase() rather than undefined normalizeNeedle(q), and that case-insensitive matching in AC-4 works for q=BAN, q=ban, q=Ban all matching name='Banana'

Verify no trimming and no regex per AC-5 by confirming the needle is q.toLowerCase() without .trim() and .includes() uses literal string matching such that q=' an' doesn't match 'banana' and q='a.c' doesn't match 'abc'
Regex Injection: Passed ?q=.*|^|$ expecting regex metacharacter execution. Code uses .includes() for literal string matching; no regex engine involved.
Prototype Pollution: Attempted dynamic property access via ?q=__proto__ and ?q=constructor. Code accesses only item.name directly without bracket notation or computed properties.

Locale-Aware Case Folding Bypass: Tested UTF-8 characters like ß where locale-aware folding would differ. JavaScript toLowerCase() applies Unicode folding consistently without locale awareness, matching spec requirement of 'no locale folding'.

The code attempts to call undefined normalizeNeedle(q), causing ReferenceError and 500 response on any non-empty q parameter; AC-1 would fail with status 500 instead of 200. The fix inlines q.toLowerCase() as the needle, making it defined and executable.

The q-filter block runs after the sort and limit cap stages instead of before them, so limit=2 truncates [banana,apple,cherry,mango] to [banana,apple] before q=an filter narrows it to [banana] instead of the correct [banana,mango]. AC-2 test would fail expecting both matching items. The fix moves the filter block before sort, restoring correct order.

Both q and item.name strings are compared without calling toLowerCase() first, so q=BAN does not match name='Banana' (case-sensitive substring test). AC-4 explicitly tests case variants (BAN, ban, Ban) and would fail. The fix adds toLowerCase() to both sides of the includes() call.
